My experience was that this clinic has problems with scheduling and managing the feelings of patients who have to wait in line.

I called to schedule a dental appointment for 2 PM.
The counter staff said there were no available slots; the doctor was only available at 1:30 PM. Otherwise, I would have to come another day.

So, I rearranged everything for the day to get a dental check-up at 1:30 PM. When I arrived at the clinic on time (1:30 PM),
the counter staff told me to wait a moment.

After 20 minutes, almost 2 PM (there were no other patients waiting in the clinic during that time),
neither of the two counter staff members informed me why my turn was delayed. They were busy chatting with patients who seemed to have already been examined, the conversation revolving around things like not chewing hard foods.

I then asked if I would be examined soon, and if so, I would go out for lunch. The counter staff (a younger one) replied:
"Please wait about 5-10 minutes. The doctor is coming from MBK."

(This is suspicious, as the doctor wasn't actually in the clinic at the scheduled time, and yet they remained so calm.) (No one informed us of anything unless we brought it up ourselves.)

We waited for another 10 minutes, until it was already 2 PM.
We still hadn't seen the doctor.
So I went to ask the counter staff (an older woman).
I explained that I had an appointment at 2 PM, but the counter staff wouldn't accept it, so they rescheduled everything until it was 1:30 PM as the clinic wanted. But the doctor still hasn't arrived, and it's now 2 PM. If he doesn't come, I'll go do something else.

The older woman at the counter replied:
"If you're going to go do something else at 2 PM, does that mean you're only giving the doctor half an hour to examine you?"
She said it irritably, even though it wasn't the point of the conversation. Then she turned to answer another phone call.
And had a younger counter staff member take over.

The younger counter staff member called the doctor again, but he still hadn't moved from MBK as he had initially said. In the end, I chose not to receive treatment there.
